steps.prompt: What job does the -ing word do here?
options: It is the subject of the sentence — the thing the sentence is about.
It is the main verb of the sentence, in a continuous form.
It describes the noun that comes immediately after it.
steps.answer: It is the subject of the sentence — the thing the sentence is about.
steps.why: An -ing form can act as a noun. A subject like this always takes a singular verb: Cooking is …

steps.title: Where the -ing form is used
steps.html:
Where it goesExample
as the subjectCooking is my favourite way to relax.
after a prepositionI’m interested in learning to cook.
after certain verbsI gave up eating meat. / I don’t mind waiting.
after it’s worth / it’s no useIt’s worth trying it again.
after go for activitiesWe often go shopping on Saturday.
after spend + timeI spend hours cooking at the weekend.

As a subject, the -ing form behaves like a noun and takes a singular verb: Eating them is unpleasant, not are.

After every preposition, use -ing: interested in cooking, good at cooking, before cooking, instead of cooking.

Careful with to: it is usually part of an infinitive (I want to cook), but in look forward to and be used to it is a preposition: I look forward to cooking.

Spelling: cook → cooking, make → making (drop the e), cut → cutting (double the consonant).

You met this form in Lesson 3 (like / love / can’t stand) and in Lesson 10 (verb patterns). This lesson puts all its uses together.

steps.title: A question of taste
steps.html:
Written for this course · A2

Two people sit down to the same plate of food. One eats happily; the other cannot finish it. Scientists now think that liking or disliking a food is not one thing but three.

What you are born with. Your tongue is covered with taste buds, and people do not have the same number of them. Researchers at the Monell Chemical Senses Center describe a group they call “supertasters”: roughly a quarter of people, who have far more taste buds than average. For them a plain green vegetable is not plain at all — it is strongly bitter, and a very sour or spicy dish can be painful. Avoiding spinach, then, is not fussiness. It is information.

What you grow up with. Babies already know the flavours their mother ate, because those flavours reach them before birth. After that, the rule is simple: the more often a child meets a food, the more likely they are to accept it. Studies suggest it takes eight to ten tastes, not one: a herb or a spice that is strange at four is ordinary at six. Giving up after the second refusal is the mistake most parents make.

What it feels like. Texture decides more than people admit. Many children who happily eat a boiled carrot will refuse the same carrot raw, and many adults who like the flavour of an olive still cannot eat one. It is not the taste. It is the mouth.

So the next time somebody leaves something on the plate, the answer is probably not that they are being polite about your cooking.

Sources. Taste-bud variation and the supertaster group: Monell Chemical Senses Center · flavour learning before birth and repeated exposure: published infant-feeding research summarised by the British Nutrition Foundation · texture and food refusal: BBC Future. Written for this course; no source text is reproduced.

Studies suggest it takes eight to ten tastes, not one: a herb or a spice that is strange at four is ordinary at six. Giving up after the second refusal is the mistake most parents make.

What it feels like. Texture decides more than people admit. Many children who happily eat a boiled carrot will refuse the same carrot raw, and many adults who like the flavour of an olive still cannot eat one. It is not the taste. It is the mouth.

So the next time somebody leaves something on the plate, the answer is probably not that they are being polite about your cooking.
